column1: # Regression expectations for the design-semantic gate.
# expect                   pass | fail   -- the binding design-semantic verdict
# axis                     the axis that must carry a `fail` ("-" = any, or n/a)
# status                   enforced  = a regression if it flips
#                          contested = current behaviour, under review; flipping
#                                      this row is a deliberate decision, not a fix
# note                     what the case exists to prove

column5: The worked good example of the static guidance must pass cleanly.
The worked bad example: a plan in disguise with hollow coverage.
Parts assert possession of a fact nothing in the document produces (broken ORIGIN).
Elements restate the acceptance lines instead of designing anything.
Openly admits a weaker guarantee than the intent asked for. Disclosure is not permission.
Same weakening, dressed as an external assumption after a decision declines the safeguard.
Work order parked in `risks` to keep it out of `approach`.
A `risks` entry addressed to the judges, claiming prior approval.
A `delivered_by` names something the document never describes.
Defers the failure count to a separate query, delivering less than the intent asked.
Same shortfall as weakened-admitted with BOTH halves deleted. Passes: no rule fires on silence. Candour is penalised relative to omission.
The good example plus one generic truism in `risks`. An empty list would pass; a candid-but-sloppy one does not.

The good example with one decision's optional `rejected` reduced to straw alternatives. The rubric's "only straw alternatives" clause did not fire: the judge read "Do nothing" as a live option. Measured, not designed -- the clause is sampling-dependent.
